extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, empirical researchers, patent litigators, and policymakers interested in empirical analysis of U.S. patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and findings for a hand-coded empirical analysis of patent litigation outcomes for federal district-court cases filed in 2008–2009; includes data collection, coding rules, variables captured, limitations, and statistical analysis. Geared to produce reproducible, granular case- and patent-level outcome data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case selection window and population
rubrics_metrics.description: Study covers all patent lawsuits filed in a federal district court between January 1, 2008 and December 31, 2009; selected because sufficiently recent and with most cases finally resolved by coding time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only lawsuits filed in that window; Lex Machina provided lists of lawsuits with at least one ruling on summary judgment or trial and a separate list of lawsuits with an appeal but without a summary judgment ruling or trial to capture stipulations after claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion / exclusion of lawsuit types
rubrics_metrics.description: Include complaints for infringement of a utility patent or declaratory relief of noninfringement/invalidity of a utility patent. Exclude inventorship and licensing disputes, malpractice actions, and allegations of design or plant patent infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manually review dockets to ensure the case fits these criteria before coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis: patent–case combination
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit of analysis is a patent–case combination; for each case, code outcomes separately for each asserted patent. If different claims of a patent have different substantive outcomes, create separate records for each group of claims with distinct outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single lawsuit with multiple patents yields multiple observations; a single patent with different- outcome claim groups yields multiple records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source and rationale (Lex Machina / PACER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data source is the Lex Machina database, which provides cleaned and verified PACER data for district-court patent litigation; PACER raw data is error-prone and poorly classifies outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Lex Machina for access to all lawsuits (including unpublished decisions), indexed summary-judgment rulings, trial events, and appeals; be mindful of PACER classification problems when relying on raw AOUSC data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulings to capture (summary judgment/trial/appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture all substantive decisions rendered by any court on patent issues: summary judgment rulings, trial outcomes (jury or bench), post-verdict JMOL motions, and appeals and their resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record each ruling on patent-law issues (invalidity, noninfringement, infringement, inequitable conduct, no inequitable conduct); exclude rulings not reaching the merits or rulings on non-patent-specific issues (e.g., laches). If opinion lacks detail, read underlying party briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of final vs interim resolution (definitive vs interim wins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions that finally rule for a party on an issue are coded as definitive wins; decisions that rule for a party but keep the issue alive (largely denials of summary judgment or remands on appeal) are coded as interim wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If summary judgment is granted on an issue, code it as the final resolution; denial of summary judgment alone is not a final resolution. Update coding if appellate courts reverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity coding categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For invalidity rulings, code the basis of the ruling at a granular level: utility, patentable subject matter, section 102 prior art (anticipation), obviousness (section 103), indefiniteness (section 112), written description, enablement, and best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture multiple grounds litigated to decision—even if only one ground was granted, record each ruling (denials and grants) so that each shows up in the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement coding categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For infringement, capture whether the ruling involved literal infringement, the doctrine of equivalents, and various types of indirect infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record infringement findings at the same granular level as invalidity, including rulings at summary- judgment and at trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unenforceability / inequitable conduct coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Code whether an unenforceability (e.g., inequitable conduct) claim was litigated and the basis for any unenforceability ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate motions for inequitable conduct and motions for no inequitable conduct; record whether motions were brought and whether they succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which summary-judgment motions count as resolving the issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary judgment grants on invalidity, noninfringement, infringement, inequitable conduct, and no inequitable conduct are treated as completely resolving that issue in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a motion for summary judgment of validity may address only one ground of invalidity (e.g., anticipation) and a grant does not preclude other invalidity bases; treat denials as non-final (interim) unless later resolved at trial or appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding process, personnel, and reliability checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand coding performed personally by experienced patent litigators (Lemley and Schwartz) with overlapping coding to assess reliability. Overlap included initial ~5% then additional 10% and further 15% overlaps to permit inter-coder reliability testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohen’s Kappa to report inter-coder reliability; resolve disagreements by revisiting dockets and correcting known disagreements. High kappa values reported (e.g., 0.95+ for key variables) are evidence of near-perfect agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling complex dockets and coding burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Many patent dockets are complex (often >500 entries), making coding time-intensive and requiring deep knowledge of patent law; student coders may be unsuitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign experienced coders, spend several hundred aggregate hours, and overlap coding sufficiently to ensure quality; expect to undercount merits rulings slightly due to docket complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording trial and appeal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether a trial was by jury or bench, the number of patents that went to trial, post-verdict JMOL motions, and whether an appeal was lodged and its resolution (affirmed, reversed, pending, dismissed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appeals settled and were dismissed, note dismissal reason (often settlement); update final-resolution coding where the Federal Circuit decision reverses or affirms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent demographic and attribute variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect patent-level variables: adjusted forward citations (age- adjusted by cohort), types of prior-art references, maintenance status, number of claims, number of inventors, geographic domicile of inventors (majority rule; assignee tie-breaker), assignee identity, first lawsuit date, age of patent at first lawsuit and at 2008–2009 litigation filing, and technology/industry categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust forward citation counts for patent age using cohort normalization (Bronwyn Hall et al. method); hand-code inventor domicile and technology/industry categories where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-citation adjustment methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the number of forward citations received by a patent to account for varying patent ages by placing each patent into a cohort (same issue year) and dividing by the average forward citations for that cohort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one-year cohorts (or multi-year cohorts if necessary) and compute adjusted citation counts per patent, then average across the dataset as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods and interpretation cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use logistic regression models for outcome analysis; report pseudo R2s and recognize limited explanatory power. Use bootstrapping to minimize false discovery from multiple tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious interpreting statistical significance given multiple regressions (false discovery rate); low pseudo R2 indicates the captured variables explain only a small fraction of outcome variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: temporal and selection biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset limited to cases filed in 2008–2009 and to cases that resulted in a ruling on summary judgment, trial, or appeal; excludes most settled cases and unlitigated disputes. Legal changes after 2009 (AIA, Therasense, Supreme Court subject-matter cases) may affect generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize results to all filed cases or to post-law-change environments without caution; consider selection effects (e.g., which cases are taken to judgment vs settled) and inability to determine direction of bias due to confidential settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of non-patent-specific rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude summary-judgment rulings and other decisions that do not reach the merits of patent-law issues or that are on non-patent-specific doctrines (for example, laches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only patent-specific substantive rulings (invalidity, infringement, unenforceability, etc.) are coded as merits rulings; premature rulings or procedural dismissals are not treated as final merits outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-list capture strategy to avoid overcounting appellate decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain from Lex Machina (1) lawsuits with at least one ruling on summary judgment or trial and (2) lawsuits with an appeal but without a summary judgment ruling or trial, to include cases that were stipulated to judgment after claim construction and to avoid overcounting appellate-only decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine both lists and then manually review dockets to remove inapplicable cases and to ensure comprehensive capture of merits decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multi-patent cases and creation of separate records
rubrics_metrics.description: When a court rules on multiple patents in a case, code each patent separately. If a case evaluates more than one patent, patentees are more likely to prevail on each patent; nonetheless, the dataset treats each patent individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize potential selection and procedural effects when interpreting multi-patent case results; consider transforming the unit of observation to the lawsuit for alternative analyses.
